P01.understanding: Buffett's folksy, rock-star public image is a projection that hides a private, emotionally stunted man, which explains how a famous figure can be isolated.
P01.cause: The public persona is a projection hiding his real private self
P01.effect: He can be isolated despite fame
wrong: Buffett's public warmth reflects his true emotional openness
Buffett is isolated because crowds avoid him
The persona was invented by the media against his will

notAsserted.text: He is the folksy, ukulele-playing grandfather of capitalism

P02.understanding: Unlike the liars, who see the island as a magical kingdom, the outsider character sees it for what it is almost immediately because he is subjected to its invisible borders.
P02.cause: He is actively subjected to the invisible borders of the island
P02.effect: He sees the island for what it really is almost immediately, unlike the liars who see it as magical
wrong: He sees the island as magical like the liars
He is fully accepted by the family
He sees clearly because he is more educated than the liars

P03.understanding: Flannery O'Connor's characters are spiritually deformed, but because that deformity is invisible we tend to excuse it, so she draws large, startling figures (her own essay's image: shout to the hard of hearing, draw large for the almost blind).
wrong: O'Connor's characters are morally good
The deformity in the characters is only physical
Readers always notice the spiritual deformity

P04.understanding: Although readers expect Darrow to love the Sons of Aries as the good guys, he genuinely hates and despises them, and sees their bombings as pointless tantrums.
P04.cause: Sons of Aries bomb supply lines or cause disruption
P04.effect: Darrow views it as a pointless tantrum (delaying terraforming)
wrong: Darrow is a loyal member of the Sons of Aries
Darrow admires their bombings
Darrow is neutral toward the rebels

notAsserted.text: these are the good guys. Darrow should love them

P05.understanding: In a red team exercise, analysts looking for contrary evidence spot an easily overlooked detail: a dog pacing the compound in satellite imagery.
P05.cause: analysts are forced to stop defending their pet theory and look for contrary evidence
P05.effect: someone notices the overlooked detail of a dog pacing the compound
wrong: The dog proves the compound is Bin Laden's
The dog was the analysts' original pet theory
The dog was found by a ground team

P06.understanding: School trains you to expect an audience because teachers are paid to read your work, producing a delusion that the world awaits your words, while in the real world your copy is invisible.
P06.cause: teachers must read your work to grade it (artificial environment)
P06.effect: you develop the delusion that the world is waiting for your words
wrong: Readers eagerly seek out new writing
Teachers read work because it is good
The delusion comes from real readers' praise

notAsserted.text: the world is waiting for your words

P07.understanding: Because humans survive by belonging to the tribe, people instinctively suppress their unique, contradictory information to fit in and keep a bond with the leader.
P07.cause: humans survive by belonging to the tribe and want to fit in
wrong: People withhold information deliberately to deceive the leader
People lack contradictory information
Suppression happens only because of fear of punishment

P08.understanding: The success-to-the-successful trap is called competitive exclusion in ecology: a runaway reinforcing loop where winners get resources to win even more.
P08.cause: Winners of a competition receive, as part of their reward, the means to compete more effectively
P08.effect: A runaway reinforcing loop in which winners keep winning
wrong: It is a balancing loop that evens out winners and losers
It applies only to taxes, not ecology
Losers receive the extra resources to catch up

notAsserted.text: What's the systemic mechanism there in ecology?

P09.understanding: Reaching the top and finding it hollow is the ultimate betrayal of the first mountain's promise; the alternative way to fall is being knocked off the mountain by failure or tragedy.
P09.effect: you get knocked off the first mountain
wrong: Failure is the only way people fall off the first mountain
The first mountain's promise is fulfilled by success
The fall is caused by choosing to leave

P10.understanding: Reading a novel makes you simulate another person's consciousness in your own mind, which is how deep reading builds empathy.
P10.cause: reading a novel means simulating another human being's consciousness inside your own mind
P10.effect: deep sustained reading uniquely builds human empathy
wrong: Empathy comes from watching films or any media equally
Reading novels only improves vocabulary
Empathy is innate and reading has no effect on it
